Balwinder Singh And Another vs State Of Punjab And Another

 At Chandigarh

 Date of decision: 04.12.2025

High Court Of Punjab And Haryana
 At Chandigarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Balwinder Singh And Another
 ...Petitioners
 V/S
State Of Punjab And Another
 ...Respondents
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Subhas Mehla

Present: Ms. Mehak Bedi, Advocate for the petitioners.
 Mr. Surinderjit Singh Nahar, Aag, Punjab.
 Mr. Kashish Thakur, Advocate for
 Mr. Angad Parmar, Advocate for respondent No.2.
 ****
Subhas Mehla, J. (Oral)
1.

Prayer in this petition is for quashing of complaint bearing No.13 dated 15.06.2022 registered under Sections 465, 466, 467, 468, 420, 120-B, 199, 200 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and all subsequent proceedings arising therefrom on the basis of compromise (Annexure P-4) arrived at between the parties.
2.
The above stated complaint was registered on the statement of the complainant/respondent No.2-Malkiat Singh.

3. On notice of motion, respondent No.2 appeared in the Court through his counsel and pleaded that he has no objection if the present complaint is quashed on the basis of the aforesaid compromise,
which has been effected between the parties.
4.

During the course of preliminary hearing, the trial Court/Illaqa Magistrate was directed to record the statements of the all the concerned 1 of 3 parties with regard to genuineness and validity or otherwise of the aforesaid compromise.

5. In compliance thereof, report from the Court of learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate,
Bholath along with statements of the parties has been received, in which, it is mentioned that the compromise is genuine and there was no undue influence or coercion from any side.

sentences.text: This Court has heard learned counsel for the parties.
7. Learned counsel for the petitioner(s) and for respondent No.2 are ad idem
that in view of the settlement effected between the parties, the present petition deserves to be accepted.

It has also come on record that the aforesaid compromise is genuine and the parties effected the same without any undue influence or coercion.
8.
In view of above, nothing remains to be adjudicated further in the present case.

Thus,
continuation of the criminal proceedings between the parties would be a futile exercise and sheer wastage of time of the Court and thus, amounts to abuse of process of law.

9. For the reasons afore-stated and having regard to the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab and another, 2012 (4) RCR (Criminal) 543 and Five Judges Bench of this Court in Kulwinder Singh and others v. State of Punjab and another, 2007(3) RCR (Criminal)
1052, this petition is allowed and complaint bearing No.13 dated 15.06.2022 registered under Sections 465, 466, 467, 468, 420, 120-B, 199, 200 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and all the subsequent proceedings are hereby quashed qua the petitioner, subject to payment of Rs.10,000/-
as cost imposed 2 of 3 upon the petitioners (i.e. Rs.5,000/- each) , to be deposited with District Legal Services Authority (DLSA), concerned.
10. Receipt regarding deposit of aforesaid cost be produced before the Court concerned.
